title: Your First Line of Code

concept.heading: What is print()?
concept.body: Every Python program communicates with you through the console. The print() function is how you make Python speak — it takes anything you give it and displays it on the screen.

analogy.heading: Think of it this way
analogy.body: print() is like texting someone. You type a message, hit send, and it appears on their screen. Python's console is just your screen — and print() is the send button.

code_example.code:
print("Hello, world!")
print("My name is Ada")
print(42)

annotations.note: print() displays text. Wrap text in quotes — these are called strings.
You can print any text you want inside the quotes.
Numbers don't need quotes. Python knows 42 is already a number.

expected_output:
Hello, world!
My name is Ada
42
key_rule: Always wrap text in quotes inside print(). Forgetting quotes is the #1 beginner mistake.

try_it_yourself.prompt: Print your name and your favorite number on two separate lines.
try_it_yourself.starter_code: # Write your two print() lines below
try_it_yourself.hint: Use print() twice — once for your name (in quotes), once for your number.
